extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants preparing a CIHR Project Grant registration (Nominated Principal Applicants and project participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step registration instructions and requirements for submitting a CIHR Project Grant registration via ResearchNet, including participant identification, proposal descriptors, summaries, budget estimate, peer-review administration, and special considerations (RCTs, clinical trials, Indigenous research, sex/gender integration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read funding opportunity and CIHR policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you have read the Funding Opportunity details and have familiarized yourself with CIHR's funding policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must review the specific Funding Opportunity and CIHR policies before beginning registration; failure to follow instructions may negatively impact evaluation or lead to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ResearchNet to prepare and submit
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use ResearchNet to prepare, finalize and submit your registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All registration activity is done in ResearchNet; technical difficulties should be raised promptly with the CIHR Contact Centre ahead of deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single ResearchNet account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You should only have one ResearchNet account. If you have already accessed ResearchNet, do not register for a new account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you use your existing ResearchNet account to avoid duplication or account conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validated CIHR PIN required for all participants
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants must have a validated CIHR PIN before starting the registration process on ResearchNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a participant's PIN is not validated, they must log in to ResearchNet, select the user tab and 'Validate your CIHR PIN' before being added by the Nominated Principal Applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizations applying as NPA must contact CIHR for account/PIN guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an organization applying as a Nominated Principal Applicant, you must contact CIHR's Contact Centre for guidance on creating a ResearchNet account and registering for a CIHR PIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Contact Centre instructions for organizational account setup to ensure correct account type and PIN validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow CIHR formatting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Please follow all instructions and requirements including CIHR's formatting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to follow formatting and instruction requirements may negatively impact evaluation and could lead to the application being withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview all components before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Please preview all components of your registration to ensure it is complete using the 'Preview' task in ResearchNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nominated Principal Applicant must preview the full registration package prior to submitting it; to mark preview complete every other task must be marked complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Consent and Submit by deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You must complete the 'Consent and Submit' section of the registration on or before the deadline posted on ResearchNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR cannot legally accept a registration until the 'Consent and Submit Application' section is completed on ResearchNet. The NPA must review and agree to conditions and consent to disclosure before clicking Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No signature pages required
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need to send signature pages to CIHR as part of the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent is provided electronically on ResearchNet; no paper signature pages are necessary at registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Paid visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Institution Paid will be able to view limited information from registration fields while your registration is in progress; full registration view will be available once submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields viewable in-progress include project title and yearly budget requested. Institutions will gain full access after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact CIHR Contact Centre for support
rubrics_metrics.description: If you experience technical difficulties with ResearchNet or have registration questions, contact the CIHR Contact Centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers available Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET; contact details provided in instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominated Principal Applicant consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominated Principal Applicant (NPA) must remain the same between registration and application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other participants can be added, removed, or change roles between registration and application, but the NPA cannot change.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVs not required at registration stage
rubrics_metrics.description: CVs are not required at the registration stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVs may be required later at the application stage; do not attach at registration unless instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant identification and role entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who initiates registration is identified as the NPA and can add participants by entering validated CIHR PIN, name, role and participant type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant types and roles include Principal Applicant, Independent Researcher (early/mid/senior), Knowledge User, Co-Applicant, Trainee, Collaborator, Other. Consult 'Determining your research career stage' for role definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title, lay title, and lay abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a project title, a lay title (clear to general public), and a lay abstract describing how the research will improve health or health delivery systems (2,000 character limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay titles and lay abstracts are used to inform the public and Parliament; these items auto-transfer to application stage but may be changed later. Lay abstract must use language accessible to a lay audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Paid selection and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the Institution that will administer the funds for your project; consult Institutional Eligibility Requirements for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the administering institution meets CIHR eligibility rules before selecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: iKT / partner / knowledge user identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the application includes a partner and/or a knowledge user (iKT projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of a knowledge user does not automatically make the application iKT-focused. If 'partner and knowledge user' or 'knowledge user only' is selected, you MUST identify at least one Principal Applicant who is a knowledge user at registration. Contributing partners must be identified at application stage only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary research location
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the primary location where the proposed research will be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the main site for research activities; used for administrative and review assignment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if this is a resubmission of a previously unsuccessful Project Grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only answer 'yes' if it is a resubmission to the same Funding Opportunity; consult Resubmissions webpage for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and ethics-related declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if proposed research involves human stem cells, human subjects, animals, biohazards (and containment level) and note certification requirements if awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects involving human pluripotent stem cells must be reviewed by the Stem Cell Oversight Committee (SCOC) prior to REB review. Awarded projects must meet Agreement on the Administration of Agency Grants and Awards and CIHR Funding Policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial disclosure and registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the application contains a clinical trial; CIHR is signatory to WHO Joint Statement requiring clinical trials to be registered and results disclosed publicly in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Tri-Council Policy Statement Chapter 11 and CIHR Policy Guide for requirements. Applicants are encouraged to use mechanisms that support efficient trial start-up (e.g., streamlined REB processes, inter-institutional agreements, participant-focused consent templates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized controlled trial (RCT) special requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the application includes an RCT; applications containing an RCT as a major component have special requirements and must be structured according to the RCT headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCT is also a clinical trial, indicate both. Applicants are encouraged to use efficient trial start-up mechanisms. See RCT evaluation criteria and headings. Failure to comply can negatively impact evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCT budget / committee selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications including an RCT as a major component have committee-selection and budget-based rules: if budget < $250,000 in every project year, you may suggest either a discipline-based committee or the RCT committee; if any project year budget ≥ $250,000 you must select the RC1 peer review committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of suggested committee, all RCT-major applications must follow RCT headings. Noncompliance can negatively affect evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Canada Section 56 CDSA exemption declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if an exemption from Health Canada under Section 56 of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act (CDSA) is required for the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Health Canada for details on obtaining a Section 56 exemption and indicate this on the registration if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Peoples research and TCPS2 Chapter 9 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if the application proposes research involving Indigenous Peoples and whether it addresses TCPS2 Chapter 9 on Research Involving First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples of Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, explain engagement with community (limit 2,000 characters), complete specified steps (answer yes to TCPS2 Chapter 9 question, provide 2000-character justification, and select the Indigenous Health Research (IHR) Committee as first suggested committee). The IHR committee may review and apply iterative peer review; at application submission you must explicitly describe community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and gender integration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if sex as a biological variable and gender as a socio-cultural factor are taken into account in research design, methods, analysis, interpretation, and/or dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, describe how sex/gender will be integrated (limit 2,000 characters). If not applicable, explain why (limit 2,000 characters). CIHR expects integration when appropriate; reviewers will assess whether integration is a strength, weakness, or not applicable and will factor this into written evaluations and overall score. Sex/gender details must be integrated into the research proposal and not only in the sex/gender textbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptors and reviewer-matching metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide keywords (descriptors), theme classifications (up to 4), suggested CIHR Institute, areas of science (primary + up to 2 additional ranked), methods/approaches (primary + up to 2 additional ranked), and study populations/experimental systems (primary + up to 2 additional ranked).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the most appropriate terms to help CIHR assign reviewers with appropriate expertise. Use reference documents (Themes, Areas of Science, Methods/Approaches, Study Populations) for full lists; rank additional selections in order of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research summary content and character limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize your research proposal using scientific/technical terms, including Background and Importance; Goal(s)/Research Aims; Methods/Approaches/Expertise; and Expected Outcomes. Completed summary cannot exceed 3,500 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sufficient technical detail to allow CIHR to determine committee assignment and reviewer matching. Failure to complete the summary will result in registration being withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total CIHR requested amount (budget estimate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the total amount requested from CIHR for the entire duration of the grant. Provide an estimate of what is required to support the research project; no justification required at registration stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may change the budget request at the Application stage. Enter the total requested amount for all project years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested reviewers (optional) and conflict avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: You are encouraged to provide the names of at least five (5) Canadian and/or international reviewers you believe have the expertise to review your application; do not suggest reviewers who are in a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR may use these suggestions during reviewer recruitment but reserves final selection. Consult the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Agreement for Peer Reviewers and Peer Review Observers for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers to exclude (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may provide names of individuals who you believe cannot provide an objective assessment and add comments specifying reasons for exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR reserves the right to make the final decision on exclusions and selection of reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested peer review committees and mandatory justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest up to two peer review committees (primary and secondary) and include a mandatory justification for each (maximum 750 characters). Suggested committees must remain the same between registration and application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR will consult committee Chairs and Scientific Officers and make the final decision on committee assignment based on the registration summary. For TAIPR (Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary) committee consideration, the TAIPR committee must be selected as the first suggested committee and justification must address interdisciplinary advancement across mandates of at least two agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific committee-based considerations (IHR, Commercialization, TAIPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications reviewed by Indigenous Health Research (IHR), Commercialization (CMZ), or Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review (TAIPR) committees will have specific considerations and may require structuring according to provided headings or undergo unique peer review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization committee applications must follow provided headings. TAIPR applications are evaluated against specific criteria within the Project Grant Adjudication Criteria and Interpretation Guidelines; indication and justification rules apply (see Committee Peer Review Guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegate access limits and management
rubrics_metrics.description: A Nominated Principal Applicant may delegate access to a maximum of five (5) individuals to support completion of tasks; delegates must have valid ResearchNet accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add delegates via Manage Access task by entering email and last name; first name optional. Access can be revoked anytime before eSubmission by selecting Delete. Delegates' access does not carry through competition phases and NPA is encouraged to remove delegates before completing Consent and Submit; if not revoked, delegate retains access in their Completed Activities tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final submission action and post-submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominated Principal Applicant must click 'Submit' to send the registration to CIHR. The application opens once registration has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required tasks are complete and Consent and Submit is done before clicking Submit. There are no signature pages required as part of the registration.
